en.name: Laksa paste
en.summary: Laksa paste is a rempah — shallot, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, chilli, candlenut and shrimp paste ground together and bound with oil. Unopened jars keep about 2 years in the cupboard. Once opened it is a fresh-aromatic paste with about 5 days in the fridge, or about 3 months frozen.
en.pantry: Unopened jars, tubs and sachets keep to the printed date in a cool dark cupboard, about 2 years from purchase — a figure taken from Thai red curry paste, which is built the same way and is the closest product with a published number. Keep them away from the hob and out of the sun. Once the seal is broken the cupboard is not an option: a paste made mostly of fresh aromatics and sitting under oil is fresh low-acid produce in an oxygen-poor environment, and it should never be left at room temperature.
en.fridge: Refrigerate as soon as it is opened, at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and use within about 5 days — the figure given for opened Thai curry paste, which is made the same way. Homemade rempah is the same or shorter. If the paste is sitting under a layer of oil, remember what that layer is: fresh low-acid produce under oil, which is exactly the situation that calls for cold storage rather than a cupboard. Use a clean dry spoon, and press the surface flat so no pieces stand proud.
en.freezer: Freezing is the practical way to keep laksa paste, and about 3 months is a fair limit — garlic in oil, the closest hazard analogue, may be frozen for up to several months. Fry the paste off first if you have time, which deepens the flavour and drives off some water, then freeze it in tablespoon portions in an ice-cube tray at −18 °C (0 °F) and bag the cubes. One cube is roughly what a pot of laksa wants.
en.thawing: Drop a frozen cube straight into a hot wok or pan; it melts and fries from frozen. If you prefer, thaw it in the fridge and use it the same day. Never leave it out at room temperature.
spoilage: Fuzzy mould on the surface or on pieces standing above the oil
A fermented, yeasty or alcoholic smell, or bubbles in the jar
A rancid, crayon-like smell from the oil
A domed lid or fizzing when the jar is opened
tips: Freeze in tablespoon cubes the day you open the jar; the fridge window is very short.
Fry the paste before freezing if you can — better flavour and less water.
Use a clean dry spoon and level the surface each time.
Never leave an opened jar on the counter while you cook.

faq.q: How long does laksa paste last once opened?
faq.a: About 5 days refrigerated at 4 °C or below. That figure comes from opened Thai curry paste; no agency publishes one for laksa paste.
Yes, and you should. Freeze it in tablespoon cubes at −18 °C for about 3 months.

faq.q: How long does an unopened jar of laksa paste keep?
faq.a: About 2 years in a cool dark cupboard, to the printed date.

faq.q: Is the oil on top of the paste a preservative?
faq.a: No. Oil over fresh low-acid aromatics excludes air, which is the very condition botulinum bacteria favour. Keep opened paste cold or frozen.

zh.name: 叻沙醬
zh.summary: 叻沙醬是一種 rempah——把紅蔥、蒜、南薑、香茅、辣椒、石栗和蝦醬一起舂磨，再用油調合。未開封的罐裝放櫥櫃大約 2 年。開封後它就是新鮮辛香料醬，冷藏大約 5 天，冷凍大約 3 個月。
zh.pantry: 未開封的玻璃罐、盒裝和調理包放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃，到標示日期為止，從購買日起算大約 2 年——這個數字取自泰式紅咖哩醬，兩者做法相同，而那是最接近且有公布數字的產品。請遠離爐火、避免日曬。封口一開，櫥櫃就不是選項：一罐主要由新鮮辛香料構成、又浸在油下的醬，等於是低酸性生鮮食材處在缺氧環境中，絕對不能放在室溫。
zh.fridge: 一開封就要放 4 °C 以下冷藏，並在大約 5 天內用完——這是開封後泰式咖哩醬的數字，而兩者做法相同。自製 rempah 一樣或更短。如果醬上面浮著一層油，請記得那層油代表什麼：低酸性生鮮食材被油封住，正是必須冷藏而不能放櫥櫃的情況。請用乾淨乾燥的湯匙，並把表面抹平，不要讓料塊露出來。
zh.freezer: 冷凍是保存叻沙醬最實際的做法，大約 3 個月是合理的上限——最接近的風險對照組「蒜頭泡油」可以冷凍保存數個月。有時間的話先把醬炒香再冷凍，風味更深、水分也少一些，接著用製冰盒以一大匙為單位在 −18 °C 凍硬後裝袋。煮一鍋叻沙，大約就是一塊的量。
zh.thawing: 直接把冷凍醬塊丟進熱鍋或炒鍋，它會邊化邊炒香。也可以放冷藏解凍並在當天用完。絕對不要放在室溫退冰。
spoilage: 醬面或露出油面的料塊長出毛狀的霉
有發酵味、酵母味或酒味，或罐內出現氣泡
油聞起來有油耗味或蠟筆味
蓋子鼓起，或開罐時冒氣
tips: 開罐當天就分裝成一大匙的小塊冷凍；冷藏窗口非常短。
可以的話先炒過再冷凍——風味更好、水分更少。
用乾淨乾燥的湯匙，每次取完把表面抹平。
做菜時不要把開封的罐子一直擱在檯面上。

faq.q: 叻沙醬開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 放 4 °C 以下冷藏大約 5 天。這個數字來自開封後的泰式咖哩醬，叻沙醬本身沒有機構公布的數字。
可以，而且建議這麼做。以一大匙為單位冷凍在 −18 °C，大約 3 個月。

faq.q: 未開封的叻沙醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 2 年，到標示日期為止。

faq.q: 醬上面那層油是防腐劑嗎？
faq.a: 不是。油蓋在低酸性生鮮辛香料上是隔絕空氣，而那正是肉毒桿菌喜歡的條件。開封後請冷藏或冷凍。
